symptoms: Global-route overflow report shows overflow concentrated in one or two rectangular regions (macro channels, between memory banks, around IO pads) vs spread uniformly across the core area — the SHAPE is the first read
Detailed-route DRC count is dominated by one layer (e.g. 90% of shorts on M4/M5) vs distributed across many layers — pin-access and track-supply problems concentrate on one layer
Post-CTS placement-utilization map is locally >85% in hot spots even when block-average utilization is in the 60s — local density, not global density, is the driver
Congestion worsens monotonically as placement utilization target is raised, but the SAME hotspot stays in the same place persistence tells you it is geometry/IO-driven, not density-driven

candidate_causes.cause: Macro pin-access fan-in (many macros on both sides of a channel escape pins onto the same track rows)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Plot the per-track overflow heatmap against macro-pin landing positions; if overflow tracks coincide with macro pin rows, this is the cause; if overflow sits between macros in cell-only regions, it is something else
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Pin-spreading on bounding macros + asymmetric channel widening toward a movable side

candidate_causes.cause: Local placement density too high (cell-spreading not aggressive enough, or density screen off)
dist
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Lower placement utilization target (typical: 5-10% drop), re-place, re-route

candidate_causes.Preferred-direction / layer-assignment m: If overflow appears on layer X even with low density, check whether the cell library's preferred direction for layer X is the bottleneck; also more pronounced at advanced nodes where the routing preferred-direction
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Layer-assignment swap (where allowed) or library swap

candidate_causes.cause: Feedthrough congestion from one block to another across a narrow channel
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If overflow tracks align with long routes going A-to-B across the chip and not with local logic density, trace the long routes; this is feedthrough, not local density
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert feedthrough buffers repower routes through wider corridors, or reshape floorplan channels

candidate_causes.cause: Hold-fix buffer insertions that were not placement-legalized
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If congestion appears late in the flow after a hold-fixing pass, compare pre-hold-fix and post-hold-fix density maps; hold-fix buffers often cluster near flops and create new hot spots
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-run placement with hold buffers treated as soft macros, or constrain buffer regions

candidate_causes.cause: Wrong congestion model vs detailed route (global route says clean, detailed route fails)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If GR overflow is <1% but DR fails badly, the global-route model is underestimating pin access or layer cost; run a quick route with a tighter model parameter
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Tighten GR model or do trial route earlier in the flow to surface the mismatch

ordering_rationale: Cheapest-first: GR overflow heatmaps and density screenshots take minutes and discriminate macro-pin vs density vs feedthrough causes before any-run is launched.
classic_trap: Lowering placement utilization when the cause is macro pin-access — wastes a 3-5 day placement re-run and does not relieve pin escape, so the next detailed route fails the same way.

symptoms: Slack distribution across failing paths: tight cluster on a shared endpoint with low sigma (~5-15 ps) vs wide spread with high sigma (>30 ps) — the SHAPE of the histogram discriminates constraint causes
Number of failing paths sharing a single endpoint, common source hierarchy, common clock, or common cell type — sharing reveals where to look first
Logic depth uniformity across failures (all paths through ~N levels, or all through one specific macro/IP) vs mixed depth — uniform depth with violations points at SDC; mixed points at placement/wire
Whether violations appeared suddenly after a specific flow step (CTS, opt, route) or were present from initial placement localizes the cause

candidate_causes.cause: SDC / constraint error (over-constrained output_delay, under-constrained input arrival, propagated hierarchical margin, wrong clock, wrong MCP/false-path categorization)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If failing paths cluster tightly on a shared endpoint with uniform logic depth, audit the SDC at that endpoint ( load, output_delay, input_delay, clock definition); a single SDC fix often clears many paths at once
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Correct the SDC entry; document with spec cross-reference

candidate_causes.cause: Logic-depth / architecture problem (combinational depth genuinely too long for the cycle time)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If failing paths through one IP/macro consistently have higher depth than neighboring logic, dump the schematic and compute available slack per gate vs worst-case path delay; architectural depth shows as uniform excess delay across many paths through the same hierarchy
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Logic restructuring, retiming, or pipeline insertion (architectural change, may not be in scope)

candidate_causes.cause: Placement / wire-delay problem (cells placed too far apart, especially on critical-path nets with poor Steiner estimation)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If failing paths have wide slack spread and wire delays on the order of the cycle time, check placed wire length on the worst nets vs estimated; particularly telling at advanced nodes where wire RC dominates
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Timing-driven placement re-run, or targeted cell moves on the failing nets

candidate_causes.cause: Clock skew / pessimism on the relevant clock domain
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If all failures share a clock domain and onset correlates with the CTS step, dump clock skew on the failing paths; skew pessimism usually produces a uniform shift, not a per-path pattern
candidate_causes.typical_fix: CTS-only adjustment or clock-buffer rebalancing (CPPR / OCV derate tuning)
fix_cost to days

candidate_causes.cause: SI / crosstalk delay degradation (glitch on aggressor nets pushes victim delay over budget)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If failures appear or worsen after SI analysis is enabled and cluster on nets with high coupled length / aggressor count, run with SI off and compare; SI typically adds path-correlated pessimism
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Shielding, net spacing, or driver strengthening on aggressors

candidate_causes.cause: Voltage / IR-drop derate pessimism (path meets timing at nominal V but not at the signoff corner with derate)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If failures only appear at the signoff corner with derate, compare nominal vs derate slack on a failing path; the gap tells you whether it is IR/derate or a real slack problem
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Reduce local IR drop (decaps, wider stripes) or relax derate assumptions with signoff justification

ordering_rationale: Cheapest-to-expensive AND highest-payoff-first: a 5-minute SDC audit that clears 300 paths beats a 3-day placement re-run; shape-of-report discrimination comes before any re-run is launched.
classic_trap: Launching a timing-driven ECO / re-placement pass before checking the SDC shape — fixes that should be 30 minutes of SDC editing become multi-day placement iterations that do not actually close the gap.

symptoms: Hold violations cluster on a single clock domain's launch-capture pair (skew imbalance) vs scatter across many domains (setup-fixing-induced short paths, or scan-shift issues)
Small negative slack (a few ps to tens of ps) vs large negative slack (hundreds of ps); small is usually clock-skew, large is usually a logic-level or routing problem
Violations appear or worsen immediately after a setup-fixing buffer insertion pass — setup fixes shorten long paths but can shorten already-short paths into hold violation
Onset correlates with a CTS update, a placement legalization, or a route update — onset localizes the responsible step

candidate_causes.cause: Clock skew imbalance between launch andops (skew is too positive on capture side vs launch side)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Dump per-path skew on failing paths; if all violations have skew imbalance pointing in the same direction and of similar magnitude, it is a CTS / clock-buffer-balancing problem; the fix is clock-tree adjustment, not data-path buffering
candidate_causes.typical_fix: CTS rebalancing (move/add clock buffers) or useful-skew optimization

candidate_causes.cause: Setup-fix ECO inserted buffers on near-critical paths that were also near-critical for hold (the same path is both barely-meets-setup and barely-violates-hold)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Diff the netlist before/after the most recent setup-fixing pass; if the hold-failing paths are exactly the ones that got new buffers, this is the cause
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Constrain the setup-fixing pass to only insert on paths with sufficient hold margin; or add hold buffers separately on the now-shortened paths

candidate_causes.cause: Short combinational path between flops (genuine logic-depth; combinational depth is too small for the clock skew + library delay)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If a hold-failing path has very few logic levels (1-2) and adding a delay buffer is the only way to close it, this is the architecture; not usually a candidate for restructuring at this stage
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert hold-fixing delay buffers

candidate_causes.cause: Hold-fixing pass using wrong corner / wrong delay cells (hold cells inserted with insufficient drive strength, or signed off at wrong corner)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare hold-fixing run settings across PVT corners; if violations clear at one corner but not another, the corner model or cell choice is wrong
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-run hold fix with correct corner and stronger / appropriately-sized hold cells

candidate_causes.cause: Scan-shift hold failures on the scan chain (capture-mode is fine; violates because of scan-only paths)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If failures occur only in shift mode (look at the mode-specific failure report), they routing or scan-buffer-balance issues, distinct from functional hold
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Scan chain reordering or scan-buffer rebalancing

candidate_causes.cause: Cross-clock hold (CDC path treated as synchronous; actually needs a synchronizer or CDC-aware hold analysis)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If failures cross async clock domains and are flagged synchronously, they should be reclassified as CDC paths and excluded from hold fixing
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Reclassify as CDC, exclude from hold report

ordering_rationale: Cheapest-first: per-path skew dump and netlist diff are minutes and discriminate CTS-skew vs setup-fix-induced vs architecture vs scan vs CDC any buffer-insertion pass is launched.
classic_trap: Inserting hold buffers on paths where the root cause is clock-skew imbalance — wastes hold cells, doesn't fix the failure regress setup on the same path.

symptoms: Setup slack degradation localized to one area of the die (vs uniform across the die — uniform points at PVT corner, local points at IR)
Dynamic IR drop correlates with switching activity hot spots (a specific clock or bus toggling heavily)
Static IR drop visible as a voltage gradient across the die from pad ring to core; the failing region is downstream of resistive power mesh
Onset correlates with a step that increased current draw (clock buffer insertion, wider buses, scan-shift activity)

candidate_causes.cause: In density in the failing region (decoupling capacitance inadequate for instantaneous current demand)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Look at decap density map in the failing region; if decap/mm^2 is well below typical the block type, this is the cause; IR drop recovery is sensitive to decap placement, not just total
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add decap cells (preferred), or widen power stripes in the region
fix

candidate_causes.cause: Power stripe / rail resistance too high between the failing region and the nearest power pad
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Static IR drop map shows voltage drop accumulating along a stripe from pad to failing cell; widening or shortening the path relieves it
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Widen stripes, add power straps, or move power pads (latter is high cost)

candidate_causes.cause: Excessive simultaneous switching on a bus / clock / control net crossing the failing region
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Dynamic IR drop map peaks coincide with switching-activity hot spots; check toggle rates on the dominant nets
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Spread switching across clock phases, add bus splitting, or insert current-shaping buffers

candidate_causes: mesh pitch too coarse for the local current demand (typical at advanced nodes where mesh was sized for average but not peak demand)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Mesh pitch and current density in the region; advanced-node IR problems are more often mesh-pitch-limited than at mature nodes
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Tighten mesh pitch locally, or add a higher metal layer strap

candidate_causes.cause: Wrong activity assumptions in IR analysis (vector set or switching probability was optimistic vs real workload)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare assumed toggle rates against measured / expected worst-case workload; if real workload is more demanding, IR is being underestimated
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-run IR analysis with realistic vectors or workload, then size stripes/mesh accordingly

ordering_rationale: Cheapest-first: decap density map and static IR map discriminate decap vs stripe vs switching causes within an hour; only after localizing the cause do you invest in a stripe or mesh rework (days).
classic_trap: Adding decap everywhere globally when the cause is a single resistive stripe — wastes cell area and may not fix the voltage gradient.

symptoms: Clock skew on a specific clock domain exceeds its target while other domains are clean — points at one tree, not global methodology
Skew distribution across a single clock domain has long tails (a few flops much worse than median) — points at placement issues (isolated flops), not the tree structure
Onset after a major placement change or a macro move — CTS usually has not been re-tuned
Hold violations concentrated on the long-skew paths of the affected domain — CTS problem shows as hold violations through skew

candidate_causes.cause: Clock buffer placement / legalization problem (buffers placed in congested regions and pushed apart, degrading skew)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check clock buffer region congestion; if clock buffers are in or near hot spots and their positions drifted from ideal, skew will be skewed
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add placement constraints / keepouts for clock buffers; re-run CTS

candidate_causes.cause: Macro / block placement unbalanced (one side of the clock domain has longer wire to flops than the other)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If flop-to-clock-buffer distances form a bimodal distribution across the tree, the source placement is unbalanced; macro / pin placement is the cause, not the tree
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-balance macro / block placement, then re-run CTS

candidate_causes.cause: Wrong clock-tree topology choice for the floorplan (mesh vs tree vs H-tree vs fishbone)
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: If skew is fundamentally limited by geometry (e.g. flops at very different distances from any single root), the topology itself is the limit; compare to alternative topologies on a subset
